Qualcomm PMIC BCL peripheral

The battery current limiter (BCL) peripheral monitors battery current and
voltage. On PMICs with an LMH interface, comparator events can be delivered
directly to LMH while selected events are also exposed to the application
processor as thermal sensors.

Required properties:

- compatible:
	Must be "qcom,msm-bcl-lmh".

- reg:
	Two address and size pairs for the BCL user ADC and LMH shadow
	peripherals.

- reg-names:
	Must contain "fg_user_adc" and "fg_lmh" in the same order as reg.

- #thermal-sensor-cells:
	Must be 1. The sensor index selects:
	  0: high battery current
	  1: very high battery current
	  2: low battery voltage ADC
	  3: very low battery voltage comparator
	  4: critical low battery voltage comparator
	  5: battery state of charge

Optional properties:

- interrupts:
	SPMI interrupts routed to the application processor. Comparators routed
	directly to LMH do not need an application-processor interrupt.

- interrupt-names:
	Names corresponding to interrupts. Supported names are:
	  "bcl-high-ibat"
	  "bcl-very-high-ibat"
	  "bcl-low-vbat"
	  "bcl-very-low-vbat"
	  "bcl-crit-low-vbat"

Example:

	bcl@4200 {
		compatible = "qcom,msm-bcl-lmh";
		reg = <0x4200 0xff>,
		      <0x4300 0xff>;
		reg-names = "fg_user_adc", "fg_lmh";
		interrupts = <0x2 0x42 0x0 IRQ_TYPE_NONE>,
			     <0x2 0x42 0x2 IRQ_TYPE_NONE>;
		interrupt-names = "bcl-high-ibat", "bcl-low-vbat";
		#thermal-sensor-cells = <1>;
	};
